core_obligations: Show that (1) implies (2) directly from the definition of geometric connectedness (proof line 948).

Assume X is not geometrically connected and use the characterization by connectedness over the separable closure to write X_{\bar k} as a disjoint union of two open, closed, nonempty pieces (proof lines 949-955).

For a quasi-compact open W, use quasi-compactness of the pieces of W_{\bar k} and the Galois action lemma to see that they are defined over a finite subextension and invariant under an open subgroup (proof lines 957-968).

Choose W_0 with both pieces nonempty and a finite subextension k' over which the decomposition of W_0 descends, and define U_W and V_W as the intersection, respectively the union, of the translates under the corresponding open subgroup H; these are open, closed, cover W_{\bar k} disjointly, and the union and intersection are finite (proof lines 970-1001).

Glue the U_W and V_W over all quasi-compact opens W to get a decomposition X_{\bar k} = U disjoint union V with U and V nonempty, closed and H-invariant, then use the descent lemma for Galois invariant closed subsets to descend to a finite separable extension k'/k (proof lines 1002-1017).
proof_roadmap: Dispose of the easy implication (proof line 948).
Descend the pieces of each quasi-compact open to a finite subextension using the Galois action on quasi-compact opens (proof lines 957-968).
Average the descent over the open subgroup to produce H-invariant open and closed pieces U_W and V_W of each W_{\bar k} (proof lines 985-1001).
Glue over all W and descend the resulting invariant decomposition to a finite separable field extension (proof lines 1002-1017).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a scheme X over a field k is geometrically connected if and only if X_{k'} is connected for every finite separable extension k'/k (statement lines 935-945). One direction is immediate from the definition. For the other, the author assumes X_{\bar k} disconnected with a decomposition into two open and closed nonempty pieces (proof lines 947-955), then manufactures a decomposition over a finite subextension: for every quasi-compact open W the two pieces of W_{\bar k} are quasi-compact and defined over a finite subextension and invariant under an open subgroup of the Galois group (proof lines 957-968), after which the intersection over that open subgroup and the union over it produce open and closed subsets U_W and V_W of W_{\bar k} (proof lines 985-1001), and these glue over all W into a decomposition of X_{\bar k} that is invariant under an open subgroup, hence descends to a finite separable extension (proof lines 1002-1017). The claim is H2: the Galois-descent bookkeeping with open subgroups is the non-formal content, while every individual input is a standard statement about the absolute Galois group.
